items.caution: Services or trusts that still depend on RC4 Kerberos tickets will fail to authenticate until they are updated.

items.title: The system must be configured to the required LDAP client signing level.
items.summary: Set the LDAP client signing requirement to at least Negotiate signing so directory queries are integrity-protected when the server supports it. Require signing may be used where the environment allows.
items.caution: Require signing will break connections to LDAP servers that cannot sign.

items.title: The system must be configured to meet the minimum session security requirement for NTLM SSP based clients.
items.summary: Require NTLMv2 session security and 128-bit encryption for NTLM-based client connections (including secure RPC), so any NTLM session this machine starts uses the strongest available protection.
items.caution: Connections to old servers that cannot provide NTLMv2 with 128-bit encryption will fail.

items.title: The system must be configured to meet the minimum session security requirement for NTLM SSP based servers.
items.summary: Require NTLMv2 session security and 128-bit encryption for NTLM-based connections this machine accepts as a server (including secure RPC).
items.caution: Old clients that cannot meet the requirement will be refused.

items.title: The system must be configured to use FIPS-compliant algorithms for encryption, hashing, and signing.
items.summary: Force the operating system to use only FIPS-compliant algorithms for encryption, hashing, and signing. The rule warns that the machine will then be unable to talk over encrypted or signed protocols to servers that do not support these algorithms. Registry location differs between Group Policy and Intune.
items.caution: Applications using non-FIPS algorithms (some .NET code, older TLS configurations, third-party tools) can fail outright; test before broad rollout.

items.title: User Account Control approval mode for the built-in Administrator must be enabled.
items.summary: Run the built-in Administrator account in UAC Admin Approval Mode so even that account has to approve elevation rather than running everything with full rights all the time.

items.title: User Account Control must prompt administrators for consent on the secure desktop.
items.summary: Make UAC prompt administrators for consent on the secure desktop when elevation is needed, so the prompt cannot be spoofed or clicked through by malware.

items.title: Windows 11 must use multifactor authentication for local and network access to privileged and nonprivileged accounts.
items.summary: Domain-joined machines must use multifactor authentication (for example a CAC with PKI) for all accounts except local emergency accounts. The check is simply that the smart card reader and smart card registry keys exist and are populated; the organization must actually enforce MFA. Not applicable to standalone systems.
items.caution: The registry check only shows smart card infrastructure is present, not that MFA is enforced; treat this as a program-level requirement rather than a single setting.

items.title: User Account Control must automatically deny elevation requests for standard users.
items.summary: Make UAC automatically deny elevation requests from standard users, so tasks needing admin rights must be started from an administrative account instead of prompting for credentials in a user session.
items.caution: Standard users can no longer enter admin credentials at a prompt; help desks must handle elevation through a separate admin session.

items.title: User Account Control must be configured to detect application installations and prompt for elevation.
items.summary: Have UAC detect application installers and prompt for elevation, so a setup program cannot silently run with admin rights.

items.title: User Account Control must only elevate UIAccess applications that are installed in secure locations.
items.summary: Only allow UIAccess applications (which can interact with elevated windows) to run elevated if they are installed in secure locations such as Program Files or Windows\System32, so a user-writable copy cannot be abused.
items.caution: Accessibility or automation tools installed in user profile folders may lose UIAccess capability.

items.title: User Account Control must run all administrators in Admin Approval Mode, enabling UAC.
items.summary: Turn User Account Control on by running all administrators in Admin Approval Mode. This is the master switch for UAC; without it the other UAC settings have no effect.
items.caution: Changing this setting requires a restart, and some poorly written legacy applications behave differently once UAC is active.

items.title: User Account Control must virtualize file and registry write failures to per-user locations.
items.summary: Enable UAC file and registry virtualization so older applications that try to write to protected locations are redirected to per-user locations and keep working instead of failing or requiring admin rights.

items.title: Passwords for enabled local Administrator accounts must be changed at least every 60 days.
items.summary: Any enabled local Administrator account must have its password changed at least every 60 days, and Windows LAPS must manage it (with 14-character complex passwords and a 60-day age) unless the AO approves an alternative. Check the PasswordLastSet date, the LAPS policy, and the LAPS operational log as described in the rule.
items.caution: Deploying LAPS requires directory schema and policy setup; without it, someone must document a manual rotation process and evidence for the ISSM/ISSO.

items.title: Zone information must be preserved when saving attachments.
items.summary: Keep Windows marking downloaded attachments with their zone of origin (the default), so it can warn about files from the internet. It is only a finding if the user policy to stop preserving zone information has been explicitly enabled; set it to Not Configured or Disabled.

items.title: The "Access Credential Manager as a trusted caller" user right must not be assigned to any groups or accounts.
items.summary: Make sure no group or account holds the Access Credential Manager as a trusted caller user right, since it could allow retrieving other users' stored credentials. The policy should be defined but left blank.

items.title: The "Access this computer from the network" user right must only be assigned to the Administrators and Remote Desktop Users groups.
items.summary: Limit the Access this computer from the network user right to Administrators and Remote Desktop Users. A domain application account for a management tool may be added if vendor documentation requires it and the exception is documented with the ISSO.
items.caution: Removing Everyone or Authenticated Users from this right can break remote management, file sharing, and scanning tools that connect with other accounts.

items.title: The "Allow log on locally" user right must only be assigned to the Administrators and Users groups.
items.summary: Limit the Allow log on locally user right to the Administrators and Users groups, so only intended accounts can sign in interactively at the machine.
items.caution: Removing a group that service or kiosk accounts belong to will stop those accounts from logging on.

items.title: The "Back up files and directories" user right must only be assigned to the Administrators group.
items.summary: Limit the Back up files and directories user right to the Administrators group, because it lets the holder read any file regardless of permissions.
items.caution: Backup software running under a dedicated non-admin account will need that account added or reworked.

items.title: The "Change the system time" user right must only be assigned to Administrators and Local Service.
items.summary: Limit the Change the system time user right to Administrators and LOCAL SERVICE, since altering the clock can break authentication and falsify event log timestamps.

items.title: The "Create a pagefile" user right must only be assigned to the Administrators group.
items.summary: Limit the Create a pagefile user right to the Administrators group, so ordinary users cannot resize the pagefile and degrade system performance.

items.title: The "Create global objects" user right must only be assigned to Administrators, Service, Local Service, and Network Service.
items.summary: Limit the Create global objects user right to Administrators, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE, and SERVICE, so ordinary accounts cannot create objects visible to every user's session.
items.caution: Some applications run under user accounts expect this right; check for them before removing.

items.title: The "Create permanent shared objects" user right must not be assigned to any groups or accounts.
items.summary: Make sure no group or account holds the Create permanent shared objects user right; the policy should be defined but blank. The right could be used to expose sensitive data through shared objects.

items.title: The "Create symbolic links" user right must only be assigned to the Administrators group.
items.summary: Limit the Create symbolic links user right to the Administrators group. On workstations with an approved Hyper-V use, NT VIRTUAL MACHINES\VIRTUAL MACHINE may also hold it.
items.caution: Developer tooling that creates symlinks under a standard account will stop working.

items.title: The "Deny access to this computer from the network" user right on workstations must be configured to prevent access from highly privileged domain accounts and local accounts on domain systems and unauthenticated access on all systems.
items.summary: Set the Deny access to this computer from the network right so the Guests group is always denied, and on domain systems also deny Enterprise Admins, Domain Admins, and the Local account group. This keeps stolen high-privilege or local credentials from being used to reach the workstation remotely. PAWs dedicated to AD management are exempt from denying the admin groups.
items.caution: Denying Local account blocks remote use of every local account, including any local admin used for support; plan an alternative before applying.

items.title: The "Deny log on as a batch job" user right on domain-joined workstations must be configured to prevent access from highly privileged domain accounts.
items.summary: On domain-joined workstations, add the Enterprise Admins and Domain Admins groups to Deny log on as a batch job so those powerful accounts cannot run scheduled tasks on lower-trust machines. Standalone systems are exempt.
items.caution: Scheduled tasks configured to run as a domain admin account will stop running.

items.title: The "Deny log on as a service" user right on Windows 11 domain-joined workstations must be configured to prevent access from highly privileged domain accounts.
items.summary: On domain-joined workstations, add the Enterprise Admins and Domain Admins groups to Deny log on as a service so those accounts cannot be used to run services on lower-trust machines. Standalone systems are exempt.
items.caution: The rule itself warns that incorrect configuration can prevent services from starting; confirm no service runs under a domain admin account first.

items.title: The "Deny log on locally" user right on workstations must be configured to prevent access from highly privileged domain accounts on domain systems and unauthenticated access on all systems.
items.summary: Set Deny log on locally so the Guests group is always denied, and on domain systems also deny Enterprise Admins and Domain Admins, so high-privilege domain accounts are never used interactively on ordinary workstations. PAWs dedicated to AD management are exempt from denying the admin groups.
items.caution: Administrators who habitually sign in to workstations with domain admin accounts will be locked out of that practice.

items.title: The "Deny log on through Remote Desktop Services" user right on Windows 11 workstations must be configured to prevent access from highly privileged domain accounts and local accounts on domain systems and unauthenticated access on all systems.
items.summary: Set Deny log on through Remote Desktop Services so Guests are always denied, and on domain systems also deny Enterprise Admins, Domain Admins, and the Local account group. If Remote Desktop is not used at all, denying Everyone is acceptable instead. PAWs dedicated to AD management are exempt from denying the admin groups.
items.caution: Denying Everyone or Local account will cut off remote desktop support that relies on those accounts.

items.title: The "Enable computer and user accounts to be trusted for delegation" user right must not be assigned to any groups or accounts.
items.summary: Make sure no group or account holds the Enable computer and user accounts to be trusted for delegation user right; the policy should be defined but blank. The right allows changing delegation settings, which could let someone impersonate other users.

items.title: The "Force shutdown from a remote system" user right must only be assigned to the Administrators group.
items.summary: Limit the Force shutdown from a remote system user right to the Administrators group, so nobody else can remotely shut the machine down and cause an outage.

items.title: The "Impersonate a client after authentication" user right must only be assigned to Administrators, Service, Local Service, and Network Service.
items.summary: Limit the Impersonate a client after authentication user right to Administrators, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE, SERVICE, and RESTRICTED SERVICES\PrintSpoolerService. The right lets a program act as another user and could be used to escalate privileges.
items.caution: Server-style applications (web or database services) running under custom accounts may need this right and will break if it is removed.

items.title: The "Load and unload device drivers" user right must only be assigned to the Administrators group.
items.summary: Limit the Load and unload device drivers user right to the Administrators group, since loading a driver is an easy way to run malicious code in the kernel.

items.title: The "Lock pages in memory" user right must not be assigned to any groups or accounts.
items.summary: Make sure no group or account holds the Lock pages in memory user right; the policy should be defined but blank. The right lets a process pin physical memory, which can starve the system and cause a denial of service.
items.caution: Some database software asks for this right for its service account; removing it may reduce that software's performance.

items.title: The "Manage auditing and security log" user right must only be assigned to the Administrators group.
items.summary: Limit the Manage auditing and security log user right to Administrators (an organizational Auditors group is also acceptable). Anyone with it can clear the security log or change audit settings and erase evidence of tampering.

items.title: The "Modify firmware environment values" user right must only be assigned to the Administrators group.
items.summary: Limit the Modify firmware environment values user right to the Administrators group, since changing firmware variables can cause hardware failures or prevent the system from booting.

items.title: The "Perform volume maintenance tasks" user right must only be assigned to the Administrators group.
items.summary: Limit the Perform volume maintenance tasks user right to the Administrators group, because it allows managing or deleting disk volumes and could cause data loss.
items.caution: Database software that uses instant file initialization under a service account will lose that capability.

items.title: The "Profile single process" user right must only be assigned to the Administrators group.
items.summary: Limit the Profile single process user right to the Administrators group, so ordinary users cannot monitor the performance of other processes to identify targets for attack.

items.title: The "Restore files and directories" user right must only be assigned to the Administrators group.
items.summary: Limit the Restore files and directories user right to the Administrators group, since it bypasses file permissions and could be used to overwrite current data.
items.caution: Backup or restore software running under a dedicated non-admin account will need that account added or reworked.

items.title: The "Take ownership of files or other objects" user right must only be assigned to the Administrators group.
items.summary: Limit the Take ownership of files or other objects user right to the Administrators group, since taking ownership lets a user change permissions on anything and then modify it.

items.title: Unused accounts must be disabled or removed from the system after 35 days of inactivity.
items.summary: Review local accounts and disable or delete any enabled account that has not logged on in the past 35 days, excluding the built-in Administrator, Guest, DefaultAccount, and the local administrator account. The rule gives a PowerShell script that lists each account's last logon. Inactive accounts that are still needed must be documented with the ISSO.
items.caution: Disabling an account that a service or rarely used process depends on will break it; confirm before disabling.

items.title: Standard local user accounts must not exist on a system in a domain.
items.summary: On a domain-joined workstation, the only local accounts should be the built-in ones (Administrator, Guest, DefaultAccount, defaultuser0, WDAGUtilityAccount) and local administrator accounts. Remove any other local user accounts; people should sign in with domain accounts. Standalone systems are exempt.
items.caution: Deleting a local account removes its profile and data; confirm the account is not in use first.

items.title: The Windows 11 time service must synchronize with an appropriate DoW time source.
items.summary: Make sure the Windows time service syncs with an authorized DoD time source. Domain-joined systems should show NT5DS (time from the domain) in the W32tm configuration output; systems that use an NTP server must point it at an authorized server through the Windows NTP Client policy.
items.caution: Pointing at an unreachable or wrong time server causes clock drift, which breaks Kerberos authentication and log correlation.

items.title: The system must be configured to prevent Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) redirects from overriding Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) generated routes.
items.summary: Stop ICMP redirect messages from overriding the routing table, so an attacker on the network cannot redirect this machine's traffic. The policy requires the MSS-Legacy templates from the STIG package.
items.caution: The setting only appears in Group Policy after the MSS-Legacy templates are installed.

items.title: The system must be configured to ignore NetBIOS name release requests except from WINS servers.
items.summary: Make the machine ignore NetBIOS name release requests unless they come from a WINS server, preventing a denial-of-service trick that floods the machine with name release requests. The policy requires the MSS-Legacy templates.
items.caution: The setting only appears in Group Policy after the MSS-Legacy templates are installed.

items.title: The setting to allow Microsoft accounts to be optional for modern style apps must be enabled.
items.summary: Enable Allow Microsoft accounts to be optional so modern (Store-style) apps that support it can use enterprise credentials instead of requiring a personal Microsoft account.

items.title: The Application Compatibility Program Inventory must be prevented from collecting data and sending the information to Microsoft.
items.summary: Turn off the Application Compatibility Inventory Collector so the machine does not gather data about installed programs and send it to Microsoft.

items.title: Windows Update must not obtain updates from other PCs on the internet.
items.summary: Set Delivery Optimization Download Mode to anything except Internet, so Windows Update never exchanges update content with random PCs on the internet. LAN, Group, HTTP only, Simple, and Bypass are all acceptable; standalone systems are checked through a different registry value.
items.caution: Choosing HTTP only or Bypass on a large network removes peer caching and increases bandwidth to Microsoft.

items.title: File Explorer heap termination on corruption must be disabled.
items.summary: Keep File Explorer's heap termination on corruption enabled (the default), so a corrupted Explorer session is terminated rather than allowed to keep running with legacy plug-ins. Only an explicit policy turning it off is a finding; set it to Not Configured or Disabled.

items.title: Windows 11 must be configured to prevent users from receiving suggestions for third-party or additional applications.
items.summary: Stop Windows spotlight from suggesting third-party apps and content to users. This is a per-user policy under User Configuration, so it must be applied to user accounts rather than the computer.

items.title: The computer account password must not be prevented from being reset.
items.summary: Do not disable automatic machine account password changes; the computer must keep rotating its own domain password. The policy Disable machine account password changes must be set to Disabled.
items.caution: Environments that clone or snapshot domain-joined machines sometimes disable this to avoid trust breakage; re-enabling it may surface those cases.

items.title: The maximum age for machine account passwords must be configured to 30 days or less.
items.summary: Keep the maximum machine account password age at 30 days or less (never 0), which is the default, so the computer's domain password rotates monthly.

items.title: The Windows message title for the legal notice must be configured.
items.summary: Set the logon message title to DoD Notice and Consent Banner, US Department of Defense Warning Statement, or a site-defined equivalent that does not alter the meaning of the required banner text.
items.caution: A custom title must not contradict or soften the banner text required by the related rule.

items.title: Caching of logon credentials must be limited.
items.summary: Limit cached domain logon credentials to 10 or fewer, which is the default. Cached credentials let users sign in when the domain is unreachable, but each one is a hash an attacker could try to crack. Only relevant on domain-joined systems.
items.caution: Setting it too low can prevent users from signing in to a laptop while off the network.

items.title: The default permissions of global system objects must be increased.
items.summary: Strengthen the default permissions on global system objects such as device names, mutexes, and semaphores, so non-admin users can read shared objects but not modify ones they did not create.

items.title: Toast notifications to the lock screen must be turned off.
items.summary: Turn off toast notifications on the lock screen so message previews and other sensitive content are not shown to anyone who walks by. This is a per-user policy under User Configuration.
